title: The Extended Diode Equation
authors: Jianhong Yang, Gonghao Sun, Tinglan Li
abstract: For more than 75 years, the p-n junction current-voltage characteristic has been derived by treating majority carriers as an inert background and conflating the junction voltage with the applied bias. Here we show that the base electric field, generated by the coupling of excess majority and minority carriers, fundamentally alters the internal potential distribution. This self-consistent framework yields a closed-form extended diode equation that reproduces the high-injection roll-off without invoking an external series resistance, thereby eliminating an empirical patch that has persisted in the classical theory.
summary: This paper develops an extended, self-consistent theoretical model for the p-n junction diode, moving beyond the limitations of the classical Shockley equation. By incorporating the electric field generated by excess majority carriers, the authors derive a closed-form equation that accurately predicts high-injection current roll-off. This provides a fundamental, parameter-free description of semiconductor device physics.
main_problem: The classical Shockley diode equation fails to accurately describe the current-voltage characteristics of p-n junctions under high-injection bias conditions, requiring empirical fixes like series resistance.
main_result: The authors derive a closed-form, self-consistent extended diode equation that accurately predicts the high-injection current roll-off from first principles, eliminating the need for empirical corrections.
method: The work employs a self-consistent two-carrier drift-diffusion framework, incorporating the electric field generated by excess majority carriers, which is neglected in classical models.
model_or_system: The physical system is the semiconductor p-n junction. The model is an extended diode equation derived from first-principles current conservation and carrier transport equations.
key_observables: The extended diode equation itself, the base electric field (splitting into ohmic and Dember components), and the universal ideality-factor crossover.
important_parameters: High-injection bias, doping concentration ($N$), and the built-in potential ($V_0$).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes a self-consistent treatment of excess majority carriers and derives the equation from first-principles current conservation.
figures_summary: Figure 2 compares the extended vs. classical J-V curves, showing separation at high bias. Figure 3 presents zero-parameter testable predictions: the universal ideality-factor crossover and the doping scaling of the onset voltage.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the failure of classical theory, introduces the self-consistent two-carrier framework, derives the extended diode equation via current conservation, and validates the results by showing recovery of the Shockley law and predicting universal crossovers.
why_interesting: The paper's rigorous, first-principles derivation of a transport equation that covers multiple physical regimes (low vs. high injection) showcases advanced non-equilibrium statistical mechanics applied to condensed matter devices.
